story: Consumer court is only for purchases above Rs 1 lakh, right? My pressure cooker cost Rs 7,800 (bought 22 Sep 2026 in Coimbatore). The lid cracked on first use and the shop refused a refund on 1 October 2026. So I can't complain?

timeline.user_words: My pressure cooker cost Rs 7,800 (bought 22 Sep 2026 in Coimbatore)
The lid cracked on first use and the shop refused a refund on 1 October 2026

evidence: Defective pressure cooker with cracked lid
facts.user_goal: To confirm if consumer court is applicable for a purchase under Rs 1 lakh and to get a refund for a defective pressure cooker
missing: Name and location of the shop
Details of the legal notice or summons (if any)

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 01 Oct 2028 (693 days left). This counts 2 years from 01 Oct 2026 (the date they refused; if they refused earlier, your deadline is earlier). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.
rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 7,800, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You can file a consumer complaint for your Rs 7,800 pressure cooker. The shop refusing a refund for a defective product is an unfair trade practice. The complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, and there is no filing fee.

claims.text: You can file a consumer complaint for a purchase under Rs 1 lakh.
A cracked lid on first use is a defect in the goods.
Refusing to take back a defective product and refund the money is an unfair trade practice.
You must file your complaint within two years from the date the shop refused the refund.

next_steps.action: Call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915 to file a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline.
next_steps.why: This is a free step that can often resolve the issue quickly.

next_steps.action: Send a written complaint to the shop's grievance officer asking for a refund.
next_steps.why: This creates a paper trail of your demand.

next_steps.action: File your complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in under the District Commission for Coimbatore.
next_steps.why: Your amount is below Rs 5 lakh, so there is no filing fee and you do not need a lawyer.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 22 September 2026 I paid Rs 7,800 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests, including on 01 October 2026, you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 7,800 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: Purchase receipt from 22 Sep 2026, Defective pressure cooker with cracked lid.

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
